name: recall probe cue list
purpose: Selects propositions to show a human coder in the source-driven recall stratum. A cue is a sampling instruction and nothing else.
may_produce: a list of propositions to put in the annotation packet
a per-cue occurrence count used to check that every cue actually occurs in this corpus
may_never_produce: an unfavourable statement about a tradition
a denominator in the design-unbiased recall estimate, which uses the random no-candidate stratum alone

matching.applies_to: the proposition text, not the window
matching.note: cues are matched with a single alternation regex; a proposition containing several cues is still one proposition and one draw

why_this_list_exists: the detector's own 53 English value patterns cannot be used to hunt for the detector's misses, because a miss defined only by the absence of a pattern is a set the pattern cannot see. These cues are independent of the value patterns: they were read off the corpus's own divine vocabulary, not generated from the rule file.
independence_from_the_value_patterns: stated as designed-not-identical, not as proven-independent. Several cues plainly overlap detector vocabulary ('gods', 'creator'); what makes the stratum useful is that a large part of it is proper names, which no value pattern matches on its own.

excluded_ambiguous_cues.sin: 3,405+ corpus hits, almost all of them the moral noun; the Mesopotamian moon god is not what the stratum is for
excluded_ambiguous_cues.set: 3,405 corpus hits dominated by the English verb; the Egyptian god reading is the rare one
excluded_ambiguous_cues.lat: a pre-Islamic goddess and an English acronym-syllable; the name is too short to carry a word-boundary test
excluded_ambiguous_cues.manat: goddess and ordinary noun in the same spelling
excluded_ambiguous_cues.woyo: appears as both a Yuman figure and an ordinary exclamation in the American-myths texts
excluded_ambiguous_cues.katcina: variant spelling of kachina; keeping both doubles the cue for one concept

verification.method: each cue is counted over the eligible passage corpus with the matching rules above; a cue that occurs nowhere in the corpus is removed from the list rather than left in as decoration

known_limitations: a cue list is English-transcription-dependent, so this stratum inherits the whole corpus's translation filter
the stratum's yield is biased toward texts that name divinities, which is why it is reported separately from the random probe and never folded into its estimate

'Sin' is a Mesopotamian moon god and an English moral noun; 'Set' is an Egyptian god and an English verb; both are ambiguous cues and the ambiguity is left to the coder rather than resolved by a regex
